# Oxygen UI component API

Generated from the `@wso2/oxygen-ui` type declarations, so it matches the installed version. Import everything from `@wso2/oxygen-ui`. Oxygen UI also re-exports the MUI components; this reference lists what Oxygen UI adds.

The tables list the props each component declares itself. Most components also accept the props of the MUI component they are built on. Storybook has examples of each component.

## Layout

### AppShell

Application frame that arranges the navbar, sidebar, main content, footer and notification panel.

Exports: `AppShell`, `useAppShell`. Storybook: App Elements/App Shell.

#### AppShell

AppShell - Convenience wrapper for building application layouts. Uses a compound component pattern where children define the layout slots. This reduces boilerplate compared to manually composing Layout components. AppShell automatically provides shell state management through context. Child components can use the `useAppShell()` hook to access and control the shell state (sidebar collapse, notification panel, active menu items).

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Yes | AppShell slot components (Navbar, Sidebar, Main, Footer, NotificationPanel) |
| `collapseOnMobile` | `boolean` | No | Auto-collapse sidebar on page load when in mobile view (default: false) |
| `collapseOnSelectOnMobile` | `boolean` | No | Auto-collapse sidebar on menu item selection in mobile view (default: true) |
| `initialActiveItem` | `string` | No | Initial active menu item |
| `initialCollapsed` | `boolean` | No | Initial sidebar collapsed state |
| `sidebarCollapsedWidth` | `number` | No | Collapsed sidebar width in pixels (default: 64) |
| `sidebarWidth` | `number` | No | Expanded sidebar width in pixels (default: 250) |
| `sx` | `SxProps<Theme>` | No | Additional sx props for the root container |

### PageContent

Content area of a page, with standard width and padding.

Exports: `PageContent`. Storybook: App Elements/Page Content.

#### PageContent

PageContent component - A container for page content with controllable max-width and centering Provides a centered content area with a default max-width of 1400px and padding of 3. The max-width can be customized and centering can be disabled if needed.

| `noPadding` | `boolean` | No | Whether to remove padding |

### AppSwitcher

Menu for switching between WSO2 applications, grouped into sections.

Exports: `AppSwitcher`. Storybook: App Elements/App Switcher.

#### AppSwitcher

AppSwitcher - Popover for navigating between WSO2 Cloud applications. A compound component pairing a grid icon button in the header with a popover listing the available platforms. The trigger renders in place; every other child goes inside the popover. Features: - Compound component pattern for maximum flexibility - Context-based open/close state sharing - Card buttons that render as links when given a `url` - Arrow-key navigation within each section grid - Responsive popover width (viewport-capped on mobile, fixed on desktop) Selecting a card leaves the popover open, since cards open in a new tab, so the current tab never navigates. The trigger, an outside click or Escape dismisses it. The current app (`currentAppId`) is the exception: it opens in the same tab, so selecting it closes the popover.

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | `string` | No | Accessible name for the popover surface (default: `"Applications"`) |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Yes | Switcher content (Trigger, Section, App, Footer) |
| `currentAppId` | `string` | No | Id of the app the user is in. Its card opens in the same tab and is marked `aria-current`. |
| `sx` | `SxProps<Theme>` | No | Additional sx props applied to the popover |
| `unavailableLabel` | `ReactNode` | No | Tooltip on unavailable cards, e.g. for localisation (default: `"Coming soon"`) |
| `width` | `number` | No | Popover width in pixels from the `sm` breakpoint up (default: 460) |

##### AppSwitcher.App

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `busy` | `boolean` | No | Shows progress and ignores clicks while an action runs, e.g. granting access |
| `component` | `ElementType<any, keyof IntrinsicElements>` | No | Custom root component, e.g. a router `Link`, for client-side navigation. Router-specific props such as `to` are forwarded through. |
| `componentProps` | `Record<string, unknown>` | No | Extra props forwarded to `component`, for routers that use their own navigation prop instead of `href` (e.g. React Router's `to`). |
| `current` | `boolean` | No | Marks this card as the current app, overriding the `currentAppId` match |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | No | Disables navigation, e.g. for platforms that are not yet available |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | No | Mark shown above the name (default: the WSO2 logo) |
| `id` | `string` | No | Identifier matched against the switcher's `currentAppId`. Not set as the DOM `id`. |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Application name (e.g. `"API Platform"`) |
| `onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement, MouseEvent>) => void` | No | Click handler. The popover stays open after it runs, except on the current app. |
| `target` | `string` | No | Anchor target (default: `"_self"` for the current app, `"_blank"` otherwise) |
| `tone` | `"platform" \| "manage"` | No | Visual treatment (default: `"manage"` inside the footer, `"platform"` elsewhere) |
| `tooltip` | `ReactNode` | No | Tooltip shown on hover and focus, typically explaining why a card is unavailable (e.g. `"Coming soon"`). Omit for no tooltip. |
| `url` | `null \| string` | No | Destination URL. The card renders as an anchor pointing at it. `null` or a blank string marks the app as unavailable: without `onClick` or `component` it renders disabled with a "Coming soon" tooltip. Only `http:`, `https:` and relative URLs are used; any other scheme renders the card disabled. |

### ColorSchemeImage

Image that switches its source between the light and dark colour schemes.

Exports: `ColorSchemeImage`. Storybook: Theming/ColorSchemeImage.

#### ColorSchemeImage

A color scheme image component that automatically switches between light and dark mode variants based on the current color scheme. Supports both automatic system preference detection and manual color scheme selection.

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alt` | `string \| ColorSchemeImageAttribute` | Yes | Alt text for the icon, can be a string or different text for each color scheme |
| `height` | `string \| number` | No | Height of the icon in pixels or CSS units |
| `src` | `ColorSchemeImageAttribute` | Yes | Source URLs for the icon in different color schemes |
| `width` | `string \| number` | No | Width of the icon in pixels or CSS units |

### ColorSchemeSVG

Inline SVG that switches between the light and dark colour schemes.

Exports: `ColorSchemeSVG`. Storybook: Theming/ColorSchemeSVG.

#### ColorSchemeSVG

A theme-aware SVG component that applies color scheme to SVG elements. Automatically maps fill and stroke attributes to theme colors for both light and dark modes. Supported color values (use with fill or stroke attributes): - `primary`, `secondary`, `accent`, `muted` - Theme colors - `text-primary`, `text-secondary`, `text-disabled` - Text colors - `background`, `surface` - Background colors - `error`, `warning`, `info`, `success` - Status colors - `border` - Divider color (stroke only) - `highlight`, `hover` - Action colors (fill only)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | No | SVG elements as children. Use this OR the svg prop. |
| `height` | `string \| number` | No | Height of the SVG. Can be a number (treated as pixels) or a string. |
| `preserveAspectRatio` | `string` | No | PreserveAspectRatio attribute for the SVG element. |
| `svg` | `ComponentType<SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>> \| ColorSchemeSVGComponentSource` | No | SVG component imported with ?react suffix, or an object with light/dark SVG components. Use this OR children. |
| `viewBox` | `string` | No | ViewBox attribute for the SVG element. Defines the coordinate system and aspect ratio. |
| `width` | `string \| number` | No | Width of the SVG. Can be a number (treated as pixels) or a string. |
| `xmlns` | `string` | No | Xmlns attribute for the SVG element. |
| `xmlnsXlink` | `string` | No | XmlnsXlink attribute for the SVG element. |

### Footer

Application footer with copyright, version and links.

Exports: `Footer`. Storybook: App Elements/Footer.

#### Footer

Footer - Application footer component. A minimal, clean footer that displays copyright information and legal links. Designed to sit at the bottom of the main content area. Features: - Copyright text with automatic year - Terms & Conditions link - Privacy Policy link - Optional version display - Custom additional links support - Responsive layout (stacks on mobile) Usage: ```tsx <Footer /** Footer - Application footer component. A compound component for building flexible footer layouts. Use the sub-components to compose your footer structure. Composition pattern example: ```tsx <Footer> <Footer.Copyright>© 2024 Your Company. All rights reserved.</Footer.Copyright> <Footer.Divider /> <Footer.Version>v2.1.0</Footer.Version> <Footer.Link href="/terms">Terms & Conditions</Footer.Link> <Footer.Link href="/privacy">Privacy Policy</Footer.Link> </Footer> ```

### Header

Application header with brand, switchers and actions.

Exports: `Header`. Storybook: App Elements/Header.

#### Header

Header - Top navigation bar compound component. A composable header component that uses the compound component pattern. Children can include Toggle, Brand, Switchers, and Actions sub-components. Features: - Compound component pattern for maximum flexibility - Context-based state sharing - Responsive layout with proper spacing - Clean, minimal design that works with light/dark themes Usage: ```tsx <Header> <Header.Toggle collapsed={collapsed} onToggle={toggle} /> <Header.Brand> <Header.BrandLogo><Logo /></Header.BrandLogo> <Header.BrandTitle>Dashboard</Header.BrandTitle> </Header.Brand> <Header.Switchers> <OrgSwitcher ... /> <ProjectSwitcher ... /> </Header.Switchers> <Header.Spacer /> <Header.Actions> <ColorSchemeToggle /> <NotificationButton ... /> <UserMenu ... /> </Header.Actions> </Header> ```

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Yes | Header content (Toggle, Brand, Switchers, Actions) |
| `minimal` | `boolean` | No | Whether to show a minimal header (hides switchers) |
| `sx` | `SxProps<Theme>` | No | Additional sx props |

| `value` | `null \| string` | No | The applied value, or `null` or an empty string when the filter is not applied. When using with Provider and the field prop, this is derived from context. |

### NotificationBanner

Banner for page-level or application-level announcements.

Exports: `NotificationBanner`. Storybook: App Elements/Notification Banner.

#### NotificationBanner

NotificationBanner - Dismissible system alert banner. A top-level notification banner that appears above the main application content. Used for system-wide announcements, maintenance notices, or important alerts that need high visibility. Features: - Multiple severity levels (info, warning, error, success) - Optional title for more prominent messages - Optional action button - Smooth collapse animation on dismiss - Full-width design that sits at the top of the app Usage: ```tsx <NotificationBanner visible={showBanner} severity="info" title="Scheduled Maintenance" message="The system will be undergoing maintenance on Dec 20th." actionLabel="Learn More" onAction={() => openMaintenanceInfo()} onDismiss={() => setShowBanner(false)} /> ```

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |

| `actionLabel` | `string` | No | Optional action button label |
| `message` | `string` | Yes | Banner message |
| `onAction` | `() => void` | No | Action button callback |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | No | Dismiss callback |
| `severity` | `"error" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning"` | No | Banner severity/type |
| `sx` | `SxProps<Theme>` | No | Additional sx props |
| `title` | `string` | No | Banner title |
| `visible` | `boolean` | No | Whether the banner is visible |

### NotificationPanel

Panel listing notifications, with tabs, actions and an empty state.

Exports: `NotificationPanel`, `useNotifications`. Storybook: App Elements/Notification Panel.

#### NotificationPanel

NotificationPanel - Slide-out notification drawer compound component. A composable notification panel that uses the compound component pattern. Children can include Header, Tabs, Actions, List, Item, and EmptyState. Features: - Right-anchored drawer that slides in - Compound component pattern for maximum flexibility - Context-based close handler sharing - Responsive width (full on mobile, fixed on desktop) - Supports temporary, persistent, and permanent variants - Can be clipped under app bar using persistent/permanent variant

|---|---|---|---|
| `anchor` | `"right" \| "left"` | No | Drawer anchor position |
| `aria-label` | `string` | No | Accessible name for the drawer dialog (default: `"Notifications"`). Override when the visible header title differs. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Yes | Panel content |
| `liveAnnouncement` | `string` | No | Polite live-region message for status updates (e.g. new arrivals or sync). List child-count changes are not announced automatically — publish here (or via `useNotificationPanel().setLiveAnnouncement`) when items arrive. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | No | Callback to close the panel (optional, uses AppShell context if available) |
| `open` | `boolean` | No | Whether the panel is open (optional, uses AppShell context if available) |
| `sx` | `SxProps<Theme>` | No | Additional sx props |
| `variant` | `"permanent" \| "persistent" \| "temporary"` | No | Drawer variant (default: 'temporary') |

### Sidebar

Collapsible application navigation with categories, items, badges and user details.

Exports: `Sidebar`, `useSidebar`. Storybook: App Elements/Sidebar.

#### Sidebar

Sidebar - Collapsible navigation sidebar compound component. A composable sidebar component that uses the compound component pattern. Children can include Nav, Category, Item, Footer, and User sub-components. Features: - Smooth width transition between expanded and collapsed states - Context-based state sharing for active/expanded states - Hierarchical menu structure with expandable sub-menus - Icon-only mode with tooltips when collapsed Usage: ```tsx <Sidebar collapsed={collapsed} activeItem={activeId} expandedMenus={expanded} onSelect={handleSelect} onToggleExpand={handleToggle} > <Sidebar.Nav> <Sidebar.Category> <Sidebar.CategoryLabel>Main</Sidebar.CategoryLabel> <Sidebar.Item id="home"> <Sidebar.ItemIcon><Home size={20} /></Sidebar.ItemIcon> <Sidebar.ItemLabel>Home</Sidebar.ItemLabel> </Sidebar.Item> </Sidebar.Category> </Sidebar.Nav> <Sidebar.Footer> <Sidebar.Category> <Sidebar.Item id="settings"> <Sidebar.ItemIcon><Settings size={20} /></Sidebar.ItemIcon> <Sidebar.ItemLabel>Settings</Sidebar.ItemLabel> </Sidebar.Item> </Sidebar.Category> </Sidebar.Footer> </Sidebar> ```

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `activeItem` | `string` | No | Currently active menu item ID |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Yes | Sidebar content (Nav, Footer, User) |
| `collapsed` | `boolean` | No | Whether the sidebar is collapsed |
| `collapsedWidth` | `number` | No | Collapsed sidebar width |
| `expandedMenus` | `Record<string, boolean>` | No | Map of expanded menu IDs |
| `onSelect` | `(id: string) => void` | No | Callback when a menu item is selected |
| `onToggleExpand` | `(id: string) => void` | No | Callback to toggle menu expansion |
| `sx` | `SxProps<Theme>` | No | Additional sx props |
| `width` | `number` | No | Expanded sidebar width |

ThemeSwitcher - UI component for theme switching Must be used within OxygenUIThemeProvider with themes prop. Default Usage (renders a select dropdown): ```tsx <OxygenUIThemeProvider themes={myThemes}> <ThemeSwitcher /> <App /> </OxygenUIThemeProvider> ``` Custom UI with Render Props: ```tsx <OxygenUIThemeProvider themes={myThemes}> <ThemeSwitcher> {({ currentTheme, themes, setTheme, isActive }) => ( <div> {themes.map(t => ( <button key={t.key} onClick={() => setTheme(t.key)} style={{ fontWeight: isActive(t.key) ? 'bold' : 'normal' }} > {t.label} </button> ))} </div> )} </ThemeSwitcher> <App /> </OxygenUIThemeProvider> ```

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |

| `children` | `(props: ThemeSwitcherContextValue) => ReactNode` | No | Optional render props function for custom UI. If not provided, renders the default ThemeSelect component. |

### TimeRangeFilter

Picker for preset and custom time ranges.

Exports: `TimeRangeFilter`. Storybook: App Elements/Time Range Filter.

#### TimeRangeFilter

TimeRangeFilter component - A button that opens a list of quick time ranges and, beside it, the fields of a custom range. Custom ranges are entered and read as UTC. The component never fetches data or clears the range itself; it reports choices through `onChange`. The button does not show the selected range: its text stays the same after a choice. Show the range yourself, for example in a chip or as text beside the button, so readers can see which range is applied.

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adapterLocale` | `Locale` | No | The date-fns locale of the date and time fields and their calendars, for example `fr` from `date-fns/locale`. It sets the month names, the first day of the week and the like. The pickers are in English when it is not set. |
| `anchorEl` | `null \| HTMLElement` | No | The element the open picker is placed under. Defaults to the trigger button. Set it when the picker is opened from somewhere else, such as a chip. |
| `applyLabel` | `string` | No | Text of the button that applies a custom range. |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` | No | Text of the button that closes the picker without applying a custom range. |
| `customRangeLabel` | `string` | No | Text of the list item that shows the custom range fields. |
| `dateFormat` | `string` | No | Format of the date fields, as a date-fns format string. |
| `dateLabel` | `string` | No | Label of each date field. |
| `fromLabel` | `string` | No | Label of the custom range start. Custom values are read as UTC. |
| `invalidRangeLabel` | `string` | No | Error shown when the custom range is empty or reversed, or a date or time is missing. |
| `label` | `string` | No | Text of the trigger button. |
| `localeText` | `Partial<PickersLocaleText>` | No | Text of the pickers' own controls (the calendar buttons, and the OK and Cancel of the dialog shown on touch screens), for example `frFR.components.MuiLocalizationProvider.defaultProps.localeText` from `@mui/x-date-pickers/locales`. |
| `maxRangeMs` | `number` | No | Longest range, in milliseconds, that a custom range may span. Unlimited when omitted. |
| `onChange` | `(range: TimeRange) => void` | Yes | Called with the new range when the user picks a preset or applies a custom range. Clearing the range is up to the consumer (for example, from the remove icon of a chip). |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | No | Called when the picker asks to close: after a choice is applied, on Cancel, on Escape, and on a click outside. |
| `onOpen` | `() => void` | No | Called when the trigger button asks to open the picker. |
| `open` | `boolean` | No | Whether the picker is open. Set it, with `onOpen` and `onClose`, to control the picker, for example to reopen it from a chip that shows the range. Leave it out and the picker opens and closes itself. |
| `panelTitle` | `string` | No | Heading of the custom range fields. |
| `presets` | `TimeRangePreset[]` | No | Presets listed before the custom range. |
| `rangeTooLongLabel` | `string` | No | Error shown when the custom range is longer than `maxRangeMs`. The default names the limit, for example 'Choose a range of at most 30 days.'; set it to translate that text. |
| `timeFormat` | `string` | No | Format of the time fields, as a date-fns format string. Keep the seconds in it: the fields pick the hour, the minute and the second. |
| `timeLabel` | `string` | No | Label of each time field. |
| `untilLabel` | `string` | No | Label of the custom range end. Custom values are read as UTC. |
| `value` | `null \| TimeRange` | Yes | The selected range, or `null` when no range is selected. The button does not display it, so show it elsewhere (for example in a chip). |

### UserMenu

Menu for the signed-in user, with profile details and sign-out.

Exports: `UserMenu`. Storybook: App Elements/User Menu.

#### UserMenu

UserMenu - Dropdown menu for user account actions. A compound component using the composition pattern for flexible menu customization. Composition pattern example: ```tsx <UserMenu> <UserMenu.Trigger user={mockUser} /> <UserMenu.Header user={mockUser} /> <UserMenu.Item icon={<UserIcon />} label="Profile" onClick={...} /> <UserMenu.Item icon={<Settings />} label="Settings" onClick={...} /> <UserMenu.Divider /> <UserMenu.Logout icon={<LogOut />} label="Log out" onClick={...} /> </UserMenu> ```

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Yes | Child elements (Trigger, Header, Item components) |

##### UserMenu.Divider

No props of its own.

##### UserMenu.Header

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `avatar` | `null \| string` | No | Avatar image URL or initials text. Image-like values (`http(s):`, `/`, `data:`, `blob:`) are used as `src`. Other strings (e.g. `"JD"`) are shown as initials. If omitted, falls back to the first letter of `name`. |
| `email` | `string` | Yes | User email address |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | User display name |
| `role` | `string` | No | Role or plan badge (e.g., "Pro", "Admin") |

##### UserMenu.Item

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `badge` | `string` | No | Optional badge/chip to display on the right |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | No | Icon to display on the left |
| `label` | `string` | Yes | Item label text |
| `onClick` | `() => void` | No | Callback when item is clicked |

##### UserMenu.Logout

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | No | Icon to display on the left |
| `label` | `string` | No | Item label text (default: "Log out") |
| `onClick` | `() => void` | No | Callback when item is clicked |

##### UserMenu.Trigger

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `avatar` | `null \| string` | No | Avatar image URL or initials text. Image-like values (`http(s):`, `/`, `data:`, `blob:`) are used as `src`. Other strings (e.g. `"JD"`) are shown as initials. If omitted, falls back to the first letter of `name`. |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | User display name |
| `showName` | `boolean` | No | Whether to show the name text after the avatar |

## Theming and providers

### OxygenUIThemeProvider

Root provider that applies the Oxygen theme and enables runtime theme switching.

Exports: `OxygenUIThemeProvider`, `useThemeSwitcher`. Storybook: Theming/OxygenUIThemeProvider.

#### OxygenUIThemeProvider

Root theme provider for Oxygen UI applications. Wraps children with MUI's ThemeProvider and CssBaseline. When `themes` is provided, enables theme switching via context (`useThemeSwitcher`). For CSP-restricted environments, pass `nonce` to apply a Content Security Policy nonce to Emotion-injected style tags, or supply a fully custom Emotion cache via `emotionCache` (takes precedence over `nonce`).

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Yes |  |
| `emotionCache` | `EmotionCache` | No | A custom Emotion cache instance, for full control over style injection (cache key, nonce, insertion point, stylis plugins, container, etc.). Create one with `createEmotionCache` (re-exported from `@emotion/cache`). Set `prepend: true` when creating the cache to preserve the previous `StyledEngineProvider injectFirst` cascade (application styles can override Oxygen UI styles). Omitting `prepend: true` changes style insertion order. Takes precedence over the `nonce` prop. |
| `initialTheme` | `string` | No | Initial theme key when using theme switching. Defaults to the first theme in the themes array. |
| `nonce` | `string` | No | CSP (Content Security Policy) nonce applied to all style tags injected by the styling engine (Emotion). Use this when your application enforces a strict `style-src` CSP directive. When provided, an Emotion cache is created internally with `createCache({ key: 'css', nonce, prepend: true })` and supplied via Emotion's `CacheProvider`. The cache is created per provider instance, so apps that mount multiple providers or remount the provider should prefer passing a module-level cache via `emotionCache` to avoid re-injecting styles on every mount. Ignored if `emotionCache` is provided. |
| `onThemesLoaded` | `(themes: ThemeOption[]) => void` | No | Callback fired when themes are loaded and resolved. Receives the array of resolved theme configurations. |
| `theme` | `Theme` | No | Optional single theme object. If provided, theme switching will be disabled. Use this for simple single-theme applications. |
| `themes` | `ThemeOption[]` | No | Array of theme options for theme switching. If provided, enables theme switching functionality. Takes precedence over the `theme` prop. |

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseDensity` | `number` | No | Particles per 10,000 px^2 (scales with screen size) |
| `clickBurst` | `number` | No | Impulse on click |
| `linkAlpha` | `number` | No | Base opacity of the lines |
| `linkDist` | `number` | No | Maximum distance to draw line between particles |
| `maxSpeed` | `number` | No | Maximum speed in px per frame |
| `mouseInfluence` | `number` | No | Radius of mouse influence |
| `opacity` | `number` | No | Opacity of the canvas |
